Uses axis=1 in groupby, tuple column selection grouped['tip_pct','total_bill'] and np.std/np.max passed to agg, which later pandas versions deprecate or remove (not stated in chapter; from 2nd-edition era API).

practices: Pass a column-name list to subset before aggregating on large data (p.293).
Use agg with a list of (name, function) tuples to name output columns, since lambdas are all named '<lambda>' (p.299).
Prefer optimized built-in aggregations over custom functions for speed (p.298).
Use group_keys=False in apply to drop the hierarchical group index (p.304-305).
Use g.name inside apply to look up group-specific values such as fill values (p.308).
Use qcut for equal-size buckets and cut for equal-width buckets before groupby (p.305-306).
Use pd.crosstab for frequency tables and pivot_table with margins=True for subtotals (p.314-316).
Use fill_value in pivot_table for empty cells (p.314).

terms.definition: Hadley Wickham, an author of many popular packages for the R programming language, coined the term split-apply-combine for describing group operations.
Because df['key2'] is not numeric data, it is said to be a nuisance column, which is therefore excluded from the result.
Aggregations refer to any data transformation that produces scalar values from arrays.
A pivot table is a data summarization tool frequently found in spreadsheet programs and other data analysis software.
A cross-tabulation (or crosstab for short) is a special case of a pivot table that computes group frequencies.
